Hi everyone, I’m planning to start working on formalizing percolation theory.

I’m aware of the existing standalone Lean 4 formalization around the bunkbed conjecture, which already develops finite independent bond percolation machinery for that project. My current interest is slightly different: I’d like to understand what reusable abstractions could eventually belong in mathlib, and then build toward a more general percolation library.

A possible direction would be to start from Bernoulli bond percolation on finite/countable graphs: configurations of open edges, random open subgraphs, connection events, connection probabilities, monotonicity, and eventually Harris/FKG-type inequalities and basic infinite-volume notions on $\mathbb{Z}^d$.

I would be very grateful for pointers to any ongoing work, relevant branches, prior attempts, or advice on the right abstraction layer, especially how to organize the graph-theoretic side versus the measure-theoretic product-space side. I’d also be happy to coordinate if anyone else is interested.
docs#SimpleGraph.binomialRandom, and maybe you can find cool things in https://github.com/YaelDillies/cam-combi/tree/master/LeanCamCombi

Be forewarned , things that you know well in pen and paper math and seem straightforward, can be very annoying in Lean. I consider percolation as one of those , and really anything that involves encoding a lot of random geometry and involves limits.

There are percolations that have phase transitions on Z, might be easiest to start there (not IID type ofc, these have marginal distributions proportional to their distance from the origin).

Thanks everyone for the pointers! After thinking about it more, I may postpone percolation for now, since it is not directly connected to what I’m currently working on. The percolation advice is still very helpful for future reference.
